readme: THE REGISTER OF GATES CI CANNOT RUN.
Every scripts/**/check-*.mjs must be referenced by something: an npm script in
package.json, a job in .github/workflows/, or an entry here. A gate referenced
by nothing is not a gate -- it is a file that once produced an answer, and it
rots without anyone noticing, because nothing ever runs it again.
check-gates-runnable-on-ci.mjs enforces that, so this file is not a list
somebody has to remember to update: leaving a gate out turns test:db red.
30 gates were referenced by nothing when this register was written, found
while fixing the runner that could not start. Ten of them needed no
credentials at all and simply had never been wired up; they went into test:db.
One was superseded and deleted. The rest are here.
THIS IS NOT A SUPPRESSION LIST. An entry must say WHY the gate cannot run
unattended and WHAT it needs, in enough detail that the next person can
decide whether the reason still holds. 'requires' names the credential,
service or process that is absent on a runner; 'run' is the exact command.
WHY CI CANNOT SUPPLY THESE. .github/workflows/ci.yml is explicit: the DB
tests run against PGlite and 'the live Supabase credentials are NOT needed
here and must NOT be added'. So a gate that reads the live database, drives
the deployed site, calls a vendor API, or needs a server on a port is out of
scope for CI by policy, not by accident. Moving one into test:db by adding
the secret would be reversing that decision, which is not a gate author's
call to make.
HOW TO RUN THEM. Locally, with .env.local present, from the repo root. They
are the pre-release sweep: run the ones touching what you changed before a
deploy, not all nineteen every time.

gates.why: Recomputes getBrokenCover's facts in independent SQL against the live database, so the TypeScript and the SQL can be compared. PGlite cannot stand in: the point is the real data.
Compiles the real getEmployeeOwnershipOverview with swc and runs it against live data, so the printed numbers are the numbers the page computes. Read-only.
Signs in as a real user over PostgREST with a genuine user JWT and reads exactly what /my-work reads. Proving RLS from the user's side needs a real user in a real project.
Follows a real /auth/callback link with a cookie jar and GETs /my-work with those cookies. The last check before handing a magic link to a human.

Asserts the working-links feature stays inside can_view_project scope, against live rows. The failure it guards -- one person's customer links rendering on another's page -- only exists with real people and real policies.

Measures that the Overview's period filter MOVES the numbers, by recomputing the bounds from time.entry and comparing against time.org_week. A filter wired to a query that ignores its bounds passes every source assertion; only data catches it.
Asks the TrackingTime API and our database the same question and prints every way they differ. Needs the vendor API, which CI has no token for and should not be calling on every push anyway.
Answers whether the view privilege fix left the org chart correct or merely empty, by counting what an employee can actually see. The question is about live row counts.

Read-only probe of Factorial's real roster against the hub. Applies a field allow-list on arrival (salary, bank, social security, disability, termination reason are dropped before anything is counted) because the API key cannot be scope-limited -- a GDPR posture that must stay a deliberate, attended run, never an unattended CI job.
Asserts the redesigned figures by GEOMETRY on the deployed site -- a chart filling its card, an area path, a donut, a gauge. A source check cannot measure dead space.
Reads the DEPLOYED management page and looks for the names. The query returning rows and the deploy reaching Ready are both true when the page is still wrong.
Drives the bottom sheet at a real phone viewport and measures its geometry against the tab bar's. Needs a browser and the app on :3000.
gates.run: npm run dev  # then: node scripts/check-mobile-sheet.mjs

gates.why: Measures document height in PIXELS across paging, because the complaint is about the height of a document. The reference implementation for browser gates in this repo.
Drives the real /people filter controls and counts the real rows, because a filter that empties the roster or folds 'no data' into '0%' is invisible in the source.
requires: the app on the SITE port

gates.why: Verifies the per-team analysis on PRODUCTION with both roles, polling for the new section's text to wait out the deploy.
Verifies the theme system and the three tabs' figures on production, in both appearances.

HTTP probe of /auth/callback against a running server, checking the guard holds against the usual bypasses. The static half of the same question is check-redirect-guard-logic, which IS in test:db; this one exercises the real route.
gates.run: npm run dev  # then: node scripts/check-open-redirect.mjs

gates.why: Simulates the GitHub Actions workflow locally -- same commands, same dummy env vars -- so a workflow change is verified before it ships instead of debugged through push-and-pray. Running it IN CI would be circular, and it runs a full production build.

Reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL out of the DEPLOYED client bundle to prove production points at the project we backfilled. Fetches public assets from the live site; there is no deployment to read during a pull request.
